name: The Constitution of the United States
desc: The supreme law of the United States, ratified in 1788. Establishes three branches of government with separation of powers and a system of checks and balances. All federal government authority flows from this document.

name: Legislative Branch — The Congress
desc: Article I branch vested with all legislative powers. Consists of the Senate and House of Representatives. Responsible for making federal law, declaring war, controlling federal spending, and conducting oversight of the executive branch.

name: Government Accountability Office (GAO)
desc: The 'congressional watchdog.' Audits federal programs, investigates waste and fraud, and reports findings to Congress. ~3,000 staff.

name: Congressional Budget Office (CBO)
desc: Provides non-partisan economic and budgetary analysis to Congress. Scores all major legislation for cost. ~240 staff.

name: Library of Congress
desc: Largest library in the world. Primary research arm of Congress. Houses 173+ million items. ~3,200 staff.

name: Congressional Research Service
desc: Provides non-partisan policy and legal research to all Members and committees. ~600 analysts.

name: Copyright Office
desc: Administers U.S. copyright law; registers claims and records transfers. ~450 staff.

name: Law Library of Congress
desc: World's largest law library; provides legal research to Congress and federal courts.

name: National Library Service for Blind & Print Disabled
desc: Provides free braille and audio materials to eligible readers nationwide.

name: American Folklife Center
desc: Preserves and presents American folk culture and the Archive of Folk Culture.

name: Government Publishing Office (GPO)
desc: Official publisher of federal government documents. Produces the Congressional Record, Federal Register, passports, and secure documents. ~1,700 staff.

name: Architect of the Capitol
desc: Maintains, operates, and improves the Capitol complex — 17.4 million sq ft of space. ~2,400 staff.

name: U.S. Capitol Police

name: Communications Division

name: Office of Professional Responsibility

name: Executive Branch
desc: Article II branch headed by the President. Responsible for executing and enforcing federal law. Encompasses the Executive Office of the President, 15 cabinet departments, and 200+ independent agencies.

desc: The central policy and management apparatus of the U.S. government. Comprises ~1,800 staff serving the President across multiple offices and councils.

name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB)
desc: Assists the President in preparing the federal budget and overseeing executive branch management. ~500 staff.
